modelIntro.title: What Is Kling 3 Motion Control?
description: Kling 3 Motion Control is a Kuaishou Kling video model for driving a still character image with movement from a reference video. The image supplies the subject to preserve, while the motion video supplies the action, body timing, pose sequence, and camera rhythm.

Use it when exact movement matters more than prompt-only direction: dance transfer, fashion movement, presenter gestures, avatar motion, product-in-hand demos, and social video variations. On Toolaze, this flow uses one character image, one motion reference video, selectable Image or Video character orientation, and 720p or 1080p output.

metrics.label: Required inputs
metrics.value: 1 character image plus 1 motion reference video

metrics.label: Character image
metrics.value: 1 JPEG, PNG, or JPG image, max 10MB; image size must be greater than 300px with aspect ratio from 2:5 to 5:2.

metrics.label: Motion reference video
metrics.value: 1 MP4 or QuickTime motion reference video, max 100MB. Image orientation supports 3-10 second references; Video orientation supports 3-30 seconds.

metrics.label: Prompt
metrics.value: Prompt is optional; use it to preserve identity, outfit, lighting, framing, and style. Keep it under 2500 characters.

metrics.label: Character orientation
metrics.value: Choose Image to match the character image orientation, or Video to follow the character orientation in the reference video.

metrics.label: Duration
metrics.value: Output duration follows the uploaded motion reference video duration instead of a fixed manual duration.

metrics.label: Motion control source
metrics.value: Pose, gesture, walk cycle, hand movement, body timing, and camera rhythm come from the uploaded video.

metrics.label: Credit guidance
metrics.value: Credits scale with the uploaded motion reference video duration; current Toolaze rate is 40 credits per output second at 720p or 54 credits per output second at 1080p.

howToUse.title: How To Use Kling 3 Motion Control On Toolaze

steps.title: Choose Kling 3 Motion Control
steps.desc: Start with Kling 3 Motion Control selected so the generator expects both a character image and a motion reference video.

steps.title: Upload the character image
steps.desc: Use one clear JPEG, PNG, or JPG image that shows the face, outfit, body shape, product, or style you want to preserve.

steps.title: Add the motion reference video
steps.desc: Upload one MP4 or QuickTime clip with the pose, gesture, walk, dance, hand action, or camera rhythm you want to transfer. Choose Image or Video orientation based on which source should define character direction.

steps.title: Set quality and refine
steps.desc: Choose 720p or 1080p. Output duration and total credits follow the uploaded reference-video length, and the optional prompt can protect identity, outfit, lighting, framing, and style.

faq.q: What is Kling 3 Motion Control on Toolaze?
faq.a: It is an image-to-video generator flow for applying motion from one reference video to one uploaded character image while preserving identity, outfit, framing, and visual style.

faq.q: Can I create from a prompt only?
faq.a: No. Kling 3 Motion Control requires both a character image and a motion reference video. Choose a standard video model if you do not have motion footage.

faq.q: Is the prompt required for Motion Control?
faq.a: No. The character image and motion reference video are required; the prompt is optional and useful for preserving identity, outfit, lighting, framing, and style.

faq.q: How many reference files can I use?
faq.a: Toolaze supports one character image and one motion reference video for this flow. The image can be JPEG, PNG, or JPG up to 10MB; the motion video can be MP4 or QuickTime up to 100MB.

faq.q: How long can the motion reference video be?
faq.a: Image orientation supports 3-10 second reference videos. Video orientation supports 3-30 second reference videos. The generated output duration follows the uploaded reference video duration.
Image orientation matches the character direction from the uploaded image. Video orientation follows the character direction from the uploaded motion reference video.
Kling 3 Motion Control on Toolaze supports 720p and 1080p output options.

faq.q: How many credits does it use?
faq.a: Credits scale with the uploaded reference-video duration. The current Toolaze rate is 40 credits per output second at 720p or 54 credits per output second at 1080p.

faq.q: Is Kling 3 Motion Control free to use?
faq.a: Video generation uses Toolaze credits. Starter credits, available settings, reference-video length, and final cost can vary by account quota and selected resolution.

faq.q: How is Kling 3 Motion Control different from Kling 2.6 Motion Control?
faq.a: Both use one character image and one motion reference video. Kling 3 Motion Control uses the newer Kling 3 motion-control model, while Kling 2.6 Motion Control remains a lower-cost nearby option on Toolaze.

faq.q: Should I choose Motion Control or standard Kling 3.0?
faq.a: Choose Motion Control when you have a motion reference video and need a character image to follow it. Choose standard Kling 3.0 when you want broader prompt-driven generation, more image references, 4K, or longer scene planning.

faq.q: How do I write a stronger optional prompt?
faq.a: Keep it short and protective: preserve identity, outfit, body proportions, lighting, camera framing, and style while following the uploaded motion reference. Remove extra scene changes that compete with the video.

testimonials.title: Creator Comments On Kling Motion-Control Tests

items.name: Maya Chen
items.quote: The image-plus-video setup makes runway motion easier to test than writing body movement from scratch. Cleaner full-body references gave me the most usable drafts.

items.name: Jordan Lee
items.quote: I used a hand-motion reference to plan how a small device should turn in frame. Keeping the prompt focused on shape, logo clarity, and lighting made the draft easier to review.

items.name: Nina Patel
items.quote: For presenter clips, matching the crop between the portrait and motion video mattered more than adding a long style prompt. The gesture stayed clearer when the reference was simple.
